The Labour Department announced today (the 10th) that its investigation confirmed Wah Sao Ice Room (Prince Edward) had provided false information to the Labour Department during its local open recruitment exercise when applying to import foreign workers. The department has imposed administrative sanctions, including immediately terminating the company's application and refusing to process any applications submitted by the company for the following year. Related report: Importing Foreign Workers｜Why were 18 cases administratively sanctioned? 1,365 complaints received in three years, about ten per cent received warnings or administrative sanctions

Wah Sao Ice Room (Prince Edward) was administratively sanctioned by the Labour Department for providing false information during its local open recruitment period.

A Labour Department spokesperson stated that following an investigation, it was confirmed that Wah Sao Ice Room (Prince Edward) had provided false information during the local open recruitment period when applying to import waiters/waitresses, junior chefs and dishwashers, thereby violating the regulations of the "Enhanced Supplementary Labour Scheme". As a result, administrative sanctions were imposed. The department has immediately terminated the company's submitted application to import foreign workers, and refused to process any applications submitted by the company under the Enhanced Scheme for the following year.

The department stressed that employers importing foreign workers must strictly comply with the requirements of the scheme, including giving priority to hiring suitable local workers. If employers violate labour or immigration laws, the Enhanced Scheme, or the standard employment contract requirements, the Labour Department will impose administrative sanctions, including terminating applications already submitted by the employer, revoking approval already granted to the employer for importing workers, and refusing to process applications subsequently submitted by the employer.

Including Wah Sao Ice Room (Prince Edward), whose sanction was just announced today, The Collective has consolidated the cases of 18 companies penalised for violating regulations on importing foreign workers. Among them, 10 companies were in the catering services and cleaning industries — why were they penalised? Of the 18 companies, 9 involved unreasonable refusal to hire local job seekers, and most were refused processing of their subsequent two-year applications to import foreign workers by the Labour Department; another two eateries dismissed local employees after importing foreign workers, resulting in immediate revocation of their already-granted approval for foreign workers.
